content: CDS design literature: alert fatigue is the primary failure mode - too many low-value or interruptive alerts cause clinicians to reflexively override even important ones. Automation bias is a documented harm: clinicians over-trust automated output and stop seeking confirmatory evidence, so a correct clinician decision can be reversed by wrong machine advice. Mediators/mitigators include showing information vs. issuing a verdict, calibrating confidence, transparency about correctness, tiering by severity, and non-interruptive delivery at the moment of decision.
